why: the C logging surface, reachable from the umbrella header since issue 0795 was fixed (`rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp` always included its C++ twin). ROS 2's counterpart is rcutils logging, which we decline as a whole -- see the log stage -- because it carries per-logger level maps, an installable output handler and a formatted-message buffer per thread. Ours emits through the platform sink the board installed. This is the entry point a C author must find FIRST: reaching for `printf` instead is fatal on Zephyr native_sim (issue 0589), which is why the umbrella omitting it was a hazard and not just a discoverability nit.
